bull_bear.body: X500 Cr equity raise at ₹57.12/share (47% premium to CMP) to fund Theme 3; X350 Cr internal accruals reinvested; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; focus on capex-driven capacity expansion, not shareholder returns; net debt-to-equity remains low at 0.16x (FY26) and targeted to fall to 0.04x by FY31.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Execution delays in Theme 3 (pellet, power, DRI) beyond Q3FY31; delays in Bindals revival beyond Mar'2028; iron ore/coal supply disruptions due to monsoon, mine strikes, or transport strikes; inflationary pressure on capex costs; regulatory delays in statutory clearances; competition from primary steelmakers if prices collapse; demand slowdown in infrastructure if government capex falters.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: The company’s ~90-day raw material inventory buffer (not finished goods) is a strategic defense against Odisha’s frequent mine strikes, transporter disruptions, and monsoon-induced ore moisture spikes — a hidden operational moat that ensures continuity, unlike peers with leaner inventories.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet at FY26 (Mar'26): net worth Rs 441 Cr, equity capital Rs 59 Cr, net D/E 0.16x; the deck frames this as 'Low leverage: Investment-grade BBB+/Stable - disciplined debt, comfortable interest coverage'.
- Credit rating BBB+/A2+ from CRISIL, Stable, reaffirmed (Jul'25) - cited as validating the credit story and enabling 'cheaper debt for incremental capex'.
- Promoter conviction cited via OCRPS subscribed at Rs 57.12 - described as a 47% premium to CMP; Optionally Convertible Redeemable Preference Shares equity conversion at Rs 57.12 happened in 2026; promoter group holds 48.9%.
- Growth funding is equity-first: fresh equity of Rs 500 Cr raised in three staggered tranches at a premium to the prevailing market price, with term debt Nil for the Rs 850 Cr project; 'Group backing: Scan Group of Industries provides a cash-flow safety net across the cycle.'
- Working capital discipline: debtor days cut from 14 to 9 (FY23 to FY26), payable days ~4, inventory days ~103 (RM ~90 / WIP ~5 / FG ~8), cash conversion cycle ~108 days, net WC ~74 days FY26; deck states inventory is raw-material-led as a buffer against ~45-day procurement lead times, mine strikes, transporter strikes and monsoon moisture.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body: - integration: backward/forward integrated across DRI, steel melting, rolling and captive power generation — evidence: "The Company has developed capabilities across various stages of steel manufacturing, including DRI, steel melting, rolling and captive power generation, enabling better integration of its manufacturing operations and resource utilisation."
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material price and availability volatility (iron ore, coal, scrap) — Fluctuations in key raw material prices and availability directly affect production costs and operating margins.
- Steel price volatility — Steel prices are influenced by domestic and global demand, imports/exports and international commodity prices, affecting sales realisations.
- Cyclicality and capital intensity of the steel business — The SWOT weaknesses flag the business as capital-intensive and cyclical, with performance sensitive to raw material prices, energy costs, steel prices and market demand.
- Energy and transportation cost volatility — Changes in power, fuel and transportation costs affect production costs and operating margins.
- Competition and import pressure — Competition, imports and changes in market demand are flagged as threats that may affect Company performance.
- Global trade and economic developments — Global trade policies, international competition and global economic conditions may affect industry margins and profitability.
- Regulatory and environmental compliance requirements — Changes in regulatory requirements and environmental compliance obligations may affect the Company's performance.
- Working-capital and liquidity risk — Receivables, inventory and payables require regular monitoring and prudent financial planning to manage liquidity.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: TMT Bars: 2.0 LTPA capacity, 82% util, branded SHRISHTII (Fe-500D/550D), Rs.43,430/ton realization; Sponge Iron: 1.5 LTPA, 84% util, 75% internally consumed; MS Billets: 2.0 LTPA, 81% util; Captive Power: 8 MW, 100% util; Pipe/Galv: 0 LTPA currently, 2 LTPA under construction; Pellet: 0 LTPA currently, 12 LTPA planned.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Described as 'Odisha's first private integrated steel producer through the secondary steel route in the mid-corporate segment', commissioned in 1996, and as Odisha's largest TMT bar manufacturer under its flagship brand SHRISHTII TMT.
- Brand-led pricing power: SHRISHTII TMT realisation shown at Rs 43,430/ton in the Odisha price hierarchy, between primary producers (est. Rs 50,000-55,000) and unbranded local (est. Rs 38,000-42,000) / spot merchant (est. Rs 36,000-40,000); the deck states the brand commands a premium of approximately Rs 1,500-2,000 per tonne over unbranded local players.
- Capital efficiency framing: 'Unlike primary producers that require large investments in upstream steel-making facilities, Scan's integrated secondary steel model delivers strong profitability with significantly lower capital deployment.'
- Distribution moat: ~99% of TMT sold direct (162,469 MT in FY26), an established multi-tier dealer/wholesaler base across Odisha with retailers contributing nearly two-thirds of sales and wholesale the remaining one-third.
- Quality credentials: IS 11786 + ISO 9001 + 14001, OHSAS 18001 certification; Fe-500/500D and Fe-550/550D grades; sizes 8mm to 32mm.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition - Bindals] Kalinga Allied Industries India Private Limited (KAII) has partnered with Scan Steels Limited to form a consortium for the acquisition and revival of Bindals Sponge Industries Limited, under IBC resolution since 2018; Bindals has a 350 TPD DRI kiln, a 12.5 MW captive power plant and five induction furnaces of 8 tons capacity to produce 1.00 Lakh MTPA of billets. SSL has infused Rs 20 Cr and KAII Rs 20 Cr toward the NCLT settlement amount, with a secured loan from Artline Commerce channelized; further overhauling, renovation and working capital to be infused 50:50 between SSL and KAII. Operations expected to resume by March 2028. A separate catalysts slide cites 'Feb 2026 - Rs 37 Cr SSL+KAII settlement by Mar 2026' and the Vision 2031 slide lists 'Bindals NCLT Integration - 350 TPD DRI + 12.5 MW + 1.0 L IF (Q4FY27)'.
- [Forward figures are estimates] The deck explicitly states 'Forward figures are management estimates, not guidance; the company expresses no view on share price.' Management estimates shown include revenue Rs 838 Cr (FY26) to Rs 1,623 Cr (FY28E) to Rs 4,133 Cr (FY31E), EBITDA Rs 49 Cr (FY26) to Rs 145 Cr (FY28E) to Rs 575 Cr (FY31E), and PAT to Rs 338 Cr (FY31E), with EBITDA margin expanding to ~13.9%.
- [Value-creation lenses] Deck presents three lenses: FY31 EBITDA potential Rs 575 Cr (DCF from the capex programme, WACC ~12%, terminal growth 4%), ~Rs 850 Cr asset base to recreate (cost to build ~17 LTPA integrated capacity at ~Rs 34,500/T plus working capital), and FY31 PAT potential Rs 338 Cr.
- [Demand backdrop] National Steel Policy targets ~300 MT capacity by FY30 (from ~200 MT) and 160 kg per-capita by FY31 vs India's ~100 kg in FY26 against world ~220+ kg; India finished-steel demand growth cited at ~8-9%; NHAI pipeline of Rs 10 L Cr through FY30 and Jal Jeevan Mission GI pipe demand named as Theme 2 drivers. Deck flags this as 'Macro context only - not a Scan forecast.'
- [Leadership succession] Promoter and Chairman Mr. Rajesh Gadodia, a Mechanical Engineering graduate from Bangalore University with 30+ years in steel; Mr. Laxminarayan Gadodia noted as next-gen 'stepping into leadership'.

Its principal products are TMT rods and other steel products, marketed under the brand name "SHRISHTII TMT", with a strong regional presence particularly in Odisha. The business is managed and reviewed as a single operating segment, closely linked to construction, infrastructure, housing and industrial sector demand.

outlook.body: Management estimates FY28 EBITDA at X145 Cr and FY31 EBITDA at X575 Cr; strategy centers on three themes: (1) Billet expansion to 3 LTPA by Sept'26, (2) Pipe/Galv plant (2 LTPA) by Q3FY28, (3) Greenfield pellet + DRI + 50 MW power by Q3FY31; no formal guidance on share price or revenue targets beyond FY31.

outlook.body: N/A (no explicit order book disclosed; demand visibility driven by ~99% direct TMT offtake via entrenched Odisha dealer network and infrastructure tailwinds)

outlook.body: Bindals NCLT revival (1.0 LTPA billet + 12.5 MW power by Mar'2028) adds inorganic scale; captive pellet plant (12 LTPA) enables full upstream control; potential replication of Odisha model in other mineral-rich states; epoxy-coated TMT and structural steel offer higher-margin product extensions.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Expanding presence in value-added and downstream steel products
- Strengthening internal and backward integration
- Modernising and optimising existing manufacturing assets
- Improving capacity utilisation and operational productivity
- Improving manufacturing and energy efficiency
- Maintaining disciplined working-capital management
- Strengthening internal cash generation
- Maintaining high standards of quality, safety and environmental compliance
- Pursuing expansion and modernisation through a combination of debt and internal/equity resources, evaluated in a phased and disciplined manner considering project viability, cash-flow generation and debt-servicing capability
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company is expanding its manufacturing platform through two ongoing projects and one revival project. At Ramabhahal Unit-I (Dist. Sundargarh, Odisha), it is establishing an MS Pipe and Structural Mill with installed capacity of approximately 2,00,000 TPA, expected to commence commercial production approximately 12 months from the report date, subject to completion and approvals. At Budhakata Unit-II (Dist. Sundargarh, Odisha), it is expanding melting and downstream capabilities with three 20 MT Induction Furnaces and one 25 MT Ladle Refining Furnace (LRF); the Punjab National Bank term loan has been disbursed and the project is progressing at a brisk pace, with commercial production expected by December 2026. Separately, the Company (via a new 50:50 promoter structure with KAI Ispat Private Limited) is reviving and modernising Scan Kai Ispat Limited (formerly Bindals Sponge Industries Limited), an acquired integrated iron and steel facility at Sunakhani, Talcher, Odisha, comprising approximately 300 TPD DRI capacity, two 15 MT Induction Furnaces, a Continuous Casting Machine and a 12.5 MW captive power plant; land is in possession and NCLT approval obtained, but substantial refurbishment is required before commercial operations resume.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's steel demand is projected to grow approximately 6.7% in 2026 to about 174.7 million tonnes, against a cautious global backdrop where global steel demand is projected to rise only about 0.4% in 2026 after a 2.6% contraction in 2025
- Global steelmaking capacity reached a record 2,445 million tonnes with estimated excess capacity of approximately 640 million tonnes and capacity utilisation around 76% in 2025, reflecting oversupply pressure on the global steel industry
- Domestic demand is supported by infrastructure development, government spending, construction activity, urbanisation and growth in manufacturing, with continued opportunities from roads, railways, power projects, renewable energy and housing
- Business performance is influenced by volatility in raw-material prices (iron ore, coal, scrap), energy and logistics costs, steel-price realisations, and global trade developments
- India's real GDP growth for FY 2025-26 was estimated at 7.6%, supporting a resilient domestic economic backdrop for steel demand
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

Its low net debt-to-equity (0.16x), disciplined working capital, and entrenched distribution channel de-risk volume-led growth in India’s infrastructure-driven steel upcycle.

segment_detail.body: TMT Bars: 2.0 LTPA capacity, 82% util, branded SHRISHTII (Fe-500D/550D), Rs.43,430/ton realization; Sponge Iron: 1.5 LTPA, 84% util, 75% internally consumed; MS Billets: 2.0 LTPA, 81% util; Captive Power: 8 MW, 100% util; Pipe/Galv: 0 LTPA currently, 2 LTPA under construction; Pellet: 0 LTPA currently, 12 LTPA planned.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body: - **steel products:** TMT rods (SHRISHTII TMT), other steel products

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- construction
- infrastructure
- housing
- industrial sectors
- India (domestic)

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: N/A (no explicit order book disclosed; demand visibility driven by ~99% direct TMT offtake via entrenched Odisha dealer network and infrastructure tailwinds)

guidance.title: Guidance / outlook
guidance.body: Management estimates FY28 EBITDA at X145 Cr and FY31 EBITDA at X575 Cr; strategy centers on three themes: (1) Billet expansion to 3 LTPA by Sept'26, (2) Pipe/Galv plant (2 LTPA) by Q3FY28, (3) Greenfield pellet + DRI + 50 MW power by Q3FY31; no formal guidance on share price or revenue targets beyond FY31.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Bindals NCLT revival (1.0 LTPA billet + 12.5 MW power by Mar'2028) adds inorganic scale; captive pellet plant (12 LTPA) enables full upstream control; potential replication of Odisha model in other mineral-rich states; epoxy-coated TMT and structural steel offer higher-margin product extensions.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's steel demand is projected to grow approximately 6.7% in 2026 to about 174.7 million tonnes, against a cautious global backdrop where global steel demand is projected to rise only about 0.4% in 2026 after a 2.6% contraction in 2025
- Global steelmaking capacity reached a record 2,445 million tonnes with estimated excess capacity of approximately 640 million tonnes and capacity utilisation around 76% in 2025, reflecting oversupply pressure on the global steel industry
- Domestic demand is supported by infrastructure development, government spending, construction activity, urbanisation and growth in manufacturing, with continued opportunities from roads, railways, power projects, renewable energy and housing
- Business performance is influenced by volatility in raw-material prices (iron ore, coal, scrap), energy and logistics costs, steel-price realisations, and global trade developments
- India's real GDP growth for FY 2025-26 was estimated at 7.6%, supporting a resilient domestic economic backdrop for steel demand

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: FY26 EBITDA margin: 5.9%; FY31 target: 13.9%; cost advantages: captive power (8 MW → 58 MW) reduces energy cost from ~₹6.8/kWh (grid) to ~₹4.0/kWh; low inbound logistics due to Odisha ore belt location; hot charging reduces billet reheat cost; brand premium of Rs.1,500–2,000/ton over unbranded local players; blended EBITDA/ton: ₹3,013 (FY26) → target ₹4,000+ (FY31)

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: X500 Cr equity raise at ₹57.12/share (47% premium to CMP) to fund Theme 3; X350 Cr internal accruals reinvested; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; focus on capex-driven capacity expansion, not shareholder returns; net debt-to-equity remains low at 0.16x (FY26) and targeted to fall to 0.04x by FY31.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company is expanding its manufacturing platform through two ongoing projects and one revival project. At Ramabhahal Unit-I (Dist. Sundargarh, Odisha), it is establishing an MS Pipe and Structural Mill with installed capacity of approximately 2,00,000 TPA, expected to commence commercial production approximately 12 months from the report date, subject to completion and approvals. At Budhakata Unit-II (Dist. Sundargarh, Odisha), it is expanding melting and downstream capabilities with three 20 MT Induction Furnaces and one 25 MT Ladle Refining Furnace (LRF); the Punjab National Bank term loan has been disbursed and the project is progressing at a brisk pace, with commercial production expected by December 2026. Separately, the Company (via a new 50:50 promoter structure with KAI Ispat Private Limited) is reviving and modernising Scan Kai Ispat Limited (formerly Bindals Sponge Industries Limited), an acquired integrated iron and steel facility at Sunakhani, Talcher, Odisha, comprising approximately 300 TPD DRI capacity, two 15 MT Induction Furnaces, a Continuous Casting Machine and a 12.5 MW captive power plant; land is in possession and NCLT approval obtained, but substantial refurbishment is required before commercial operations resume.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body: - integration: backward/forward integrated across DRI, steel melting, rolling and captive power generation — evidence: "The Company has developed capabilities across various stages of steel manufacturing, including DRI, steel melting, rolling and captive power generation, enabling better integration of its manufacturing operations and resource utilisation."

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Execution delays in Theme 3 (pellet, power, DRI) beyond Q3FY31; delays in Bindals revival beyond Mar'2028; iron ore/coal supply disruptions due to monsoon, mine strikes, or transport strikes; inflationary pressure on capex costs; regulatory delays in statutory clearances; competition from primary steelmakers if prices collapse; demand slowdown in infrastructure if government capex falters.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The company’s ~90-day raw material inventory buffer (not finished goods) is a strategic defense against Odisha’s frequent mine strikes, transporter disruptions, and monsoon-induced ore moisture spikes — a hidden operational moat that ensures continuity, unlike peers with leaner inventories.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Expanding presence in value-added and downstream steel products
- Strengthening internal and backward integration
- Modernising and optimising existing manufacturing assets
- Improving capacity utilisation and operational productivity
- Improving manufacturing and energy efficiency
- Maintaining disciplined working-capital management
- Strengthening internal cash generation
- Maintaining high standards of quality, safety and environmental compliance
- Pursuing expansion and modernisation through a combination of debt and internal/equity resources, evaluated in a phased and disciplined manner considering …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition - Bindals] Kalinga Allied Industries India Private Limited (KAII) has partnered with Scan Steels Limited to form a consortium for the acquisition and revival of Bindals Sponge Industries Limited, under IBC resolution since 2018; Bindals has a 350 TPD DRI kiln, a 12.5 MW captive power plant and five induction furnaces of 8 tons capacity to produce 1.00 Lakh MTPA of billets. SSL has infused Rs 20 Cr and KAII Rs 20 Cr toward the NCLT settlement amount, with a secured loan from Artline Commerce channelized; further overhauling, renovation and working capital to be infused 50:50 between SSL and KAII. Operations expected to resume by March 2028. A separate catalysts slide cites 'Feb 2026 - Rs 37 Cr SSL+KAII settlement by Mar 2026' and the Vision 2031 slide lists 'Bindals NCLT Integration - 350 TPD DRI + 12.5 MW + 1.0 L IF (Q4FY27)'.
- [Forward figures are estimates] The deck explicitly states 'Forward figures are management estimates, not guidance; the company expresses no view on share price.' Management estimates shown include revenue Rs 838 Cr (FY26) to Rs 1,623 Cr (FY28E) to Rs 4,133 Cr (FY31E), EBITDA Rs 49 Cr (FY26) to Rs 145 Cr (FY28E) to Rs 575 Cr (FY31E), and PAT to Rs 338 Cr (FY31E), with EBITDA margin expanding to ~13.9%.
- [Value-creation lenses] Deck presents three lenses: FY31 EBITDA potential Rs 575 Cr (DCF from the capex programme, WACC ~12%, terminal growth 4%), ~Rs 850 Cr asset base to recreate (cost to build ~17 LTPA integrated capacity at ~Rs 34,500/T plus working capital), and FY31 PAT potential Rs 338 Cr.
- [Demand backdrop] National Steel Policy targets ~300 MT capacity by FY30 (from ~200 MT) and 160 kg per-capita by FY31 vs India's ~100 kg in FY26 against world ~220+ kg; India finished-steel demand growth cited at ~8-9%; NHAI pipeline of Rs 10 L Cr through FY30 and Jal Jeevan Mission GI pipe demand named as Theme 2 drivers. Deck flags this as 'Macro context only - not a Scan forecast.'
- [Leadership succession] Promoter and Chairman Mr. Rajesh Gadodia, a Mechanical Engineering graduate from Bangalore University with 30+ years in steel; Mr. Laxminarayan Gadodia noted as next-gen 'stepping into leadership'.

themes.title: Metals & mining cycle - steel, aluminium, critical minerals
themes.need: Domestic demand growth, safeguard duties and an India capacity-expansion wave lift integrated metals while critical-mineral security gains policy support. TATASTEEL targets 45-50 MT India (FY26 India EBITDA INR34,272cr at 24% margin) with a +INR6,000/t 1QFY27 realisation uplift; JINDALSTEL/SAIL/JSWSTEEL-tier on steel; HINDALCO/NALCO on aluminium; HINDZINC on zinc (Q1FY27 all-time-record EBITDA INR8,074cr +109% YoY on a record-low zinc cost-of-production USD851/t, though CEO Arun Misra hands over to ex-SAIL chief Amarendu Prakash 1-Aug-2026 and a new Gundlupet REE/Yttrium critical-minerals block won this quarter is a 2031-32-dated option, not near-term); NMDC/COALINDIA/LLOYDSME/SARDAEN on iron-ore/coal/integrated mining. Q1FY27 also quantified the export-side shock and the downstream escape from it: JINDALSAW's consolidated PAT fell 78% YoY to INR 91cr on +9% revenue because the Strait-of-Hormuz blockade suspended ALL India-origin MENA export shipments from March 2026, holding utilisation at ~60-65%; SHYAMMETL took the other route, posting INR 5,455cr revenue (+23.3%) at a multi-quarter-high 14.9% EBITDA margin with aluminium EBITDA/t +52% YoY and specialty alloys near 20.5% margin, self-funding ~INR 9,580cr of balance capex with no debt.
themes.driver: Steel price/realisation uplift into Q1; safeguard-duty support; Hormuz reopening for line-pipe exports; value-added/downstream mix; iron-ore + critical-mineral volume ramp.
